semin-durr:1-1.t:
Al-Kisāʾī read {أرَيْتَ} with the hamza dropped. Its verification was given earlier in Sūrat al-Anʿām. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not the preferred reading, because dropping it is restricted to the imperfect, and «rayta» is not sound from the Arabs. What made it easier is the occurrence of the interrogative particle at the beginning of the sentence, and the like of it is:
4656 - صاحِ هل رَيْتَ أو سَمِعْتَ براعٍ ... رَدَّ في الضَّرْعِ ما قرى في العِلابِ
(O friend, have you seen or heard of a herdsman who put back into the udder what was gathered in the milk-bowls?)"
In this «أَرَأَيْتَ» there are two views. The first: that it is of sight (baṣariyya), so it takes one object, which is the relative noun, as if he had said: "have you seen the one who denies?" The second: that it has the meaning of "tell me", so it takes two objects; al-Ḥawfī implied it as "is he not deserving of punishment?", and al-Zamakhsharī as "who is he?". What shows this is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, «أَرَأَيْتَك» with the kāf of address, for the kāf does not attach to the verb of sight.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {فَذَلِكَ}: there are two views on it. The first: that the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition, that is: "if you consider him, or if you seek knowledge of him, then that (is he)". The second: that it is a conjunction, «فذلك» being conjoined to «الذي يَكَذِّبُ», either as a conjoining of one entity to another entity or of one attribute to another attribute, and the answer of «أَرَأَيْتَ» is omitted because what follows indicates it, as if it had been said: "Tell me, and what do you say of the one who denies the recompense, and of the one who mistreats the orphan and does not feed the poor: is what he does good?" On the first view the demonstrative is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the relative noun after it is the khabar, or it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "he is that one", and the relative noun is its adjective (naʿt). On the second view it is accusative, being conjoined to what is accusative.
But the Shaykh rejected the second, saying: "So he made «ذلك» in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the object. This is an odd construction, like your saying 'I honoured the one who visits us, and that one who is kind to us'; what comes to mind first is that «فذلك» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ. On the supposition of the accusative the implied form would be: 'I honoured the one who visits us, so I honoured that one who is kind to us.' The demonstrative in this supposition is not as firmly placed as what is eloquent, for there is no need to point to the one who visits us; rather, the eloquent form is: 'I honoured the one who visits us, and the one who is kind to us', or 'I honoured the one who visits us, so he is kind to us'. As for his saying 'either a conjoining of one entity to another entity', it is not sound, because «فذلك» is a pointing to «الذي يُكَذِّب», so they are not two entities, since what is pointed to by «ذلك» is one. As for his saying 'the answer of «أرأيتَ» is omitted', this is not called an answer; rather, it is in the position of the second object of «أرأيتَ». As for his implying 'is what he does good?', we do not know the interrogative hamza to enter «niʿma» or «biʾsa», for they are both declarations of praise or blame (inshāʾ), and the interrogative enters only on a report (khabar)." End of quotation.
The reply to his saying "the demonstrative is not firmly placed" and so on is that the difference between the two is that in the noble verse there is an interrogative, namely «أرأيتَ», so it is good that it should explain what is asked about, unlike the example he gave; hence the stated construction is good. And to his saying "because «فذلك» is a pointing to «الذي يُكَذِّب»", by refusal: rather it points to what comes after it, as you say "Strike Zayd, and that standing one", a pointing to the standing one and not to Zayd, though it may be a pointing to him. And to his saying "it is not called an answer": the grammarians say "the answer of the interrogative", and this has been preceded by an interrogative, so that is good. And to his saying "the interrogative enters only on a report": by counter-argument with His saying {فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ} [Muḥammad: 22], for «ʿasā» is an inshāʾ, and what is a valid answer for him is a valid answer for us.
The majority read with ḍamma on the dāl and shadda on the ʿayn, from «daʿʿahu», that is, he pushed him away. The Commander of the Believers, al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read «يَدَعُ» with fatḥa on the dāl and without shadda on the ʿayn, that is, he leaves and neglects. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ولا يُحاضُّ», from «muḥāḍḍa», which was treated in [Sūrat] al-Fajr.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ}: the khabar of His saying «فوَيْلٌ»; the fāʾ is for causation (li-l-tasabbub), that is: from these blameworthy attributes follows the invocation of woe upon them. Al-Zamakhsharī said, after his saying "as if it had been said: 'tell me, and what do you say of the one who denies the religion', up to 'is what he does good?'": "Then Allah the Exalted said {فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ}, that is, when it is known that he is an evildoer: woe to the worshippers, in the sense 'woe to them', except that He put their attribute in the place of their pronoun, because they were, together with the denial and what is annexed to it, heedless of the prayer, showing off, not paying zakāt on their wealth. If you ask: how did you make «المُصَلِّين» stand in the place of the pronoun of 'the one who denies', who is singular? I say: because its meaning is plural, since what is meant by it is the kind (al-jins)."
The Shaykh said: "As for his putting «المُصَلِّين» in the place of the pronoun, and «المُصَلِّين» being plural because the pronoun of 'the one who denies' is plural in meaning, it is an evident affectation. The Qurʾān should be taken only on what the apparent sense gives, and it is the habit of this man to affect things in understanding the Qurʾān that are not clear." End of quotation. I say: it is the habit of our Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, to be biased against al-Zamakhsharī until he makes his good appear ugly. How can what he said be rejected, when it has the interlinking of the discourse, each part to the other, making it a single thing, and the intensification of the threat that it contains in bringing out their shameful description? There is no doubt that the apparent sense of the discourse is that the whole sūra describes a people who combined all of these attributes: denying the religion, repelling the orphan, not urging the feeding of the poor, heedlessness in prayer, showing off, and withholding what is good.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {الذين هُمْ}: it may be in the position of the nominative, or the accusative, or the genitive as a follower, either an adjective (naʿt), a badal or a bayān; likewise the second relative noun, except that it may be a follower of «المُصَلِّيْنَ» or a follower of the first relative noun. His saying «يُراؤُون»: its original is «yurāʾiyūna», like «yuqātilūna». The meaning of murāʾāt is that the one who shows off (al-murāʾī) shows people his deed, and they show him praise of it, so the reciprocity (mufāʿala) in it is clear. The verification of this was given earlier.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {الماعون}: there are several views. The first: that it is of the form fāʿūl from «al-maʿn», which is the little thing. One says «māluhu maʿna», that is, little; Quṭrub said this. The second: that it is a passive participle of «aʿānahu, yuʿīnuhu»; the original is «maʿwūn». On this it ought by right to be said «maʿūn», like «maqūl» and «maṣūn», passive participles of «qāla» and «ṣāna», but the word was inverted, its ʿayn being put before its fāʾ, so that it became «mawʿūn»; then the first wāw was changed to alif, as they say «tāba» and «ṣāma» for «tawba» and «ṣawma», so its pattern is now «maʿfūl» [Translator's note: so printed in the source, evidently «mafʿūl» in its inverted form]. In this view there is irregularity in three respects. The first: that a form mafʿūl has come from af ʿala, whereas by right it should be on mufʿal, like mukram, so that one would say «muʿān», like «muqām»; mafʿūl is the passive participle of the triliteral. The second: the inversion, which is contrary to the original. The third: changing the weak letter to alif although it is not vowelled, and analogizing it on «tāba» and «ṣāma» is remote, because of the irregularity of what is analogized upon. The third may be answered by saying that the wāw was vowelled in the original before the inversion, since it is on the pattern of «maʿwūn».
The third of the first views: that its original is «maʿūna» and the alif is a replacement for the hāʾ; its pattern is «mafʿul», like «malūm», and its pattern after the addition is «mā fuʿl». The expressions of the commentators differed on it, and the best of them is that it is everything that is used for help and benefit, like the axe, the bucket and the fire-striker. The saying of al-Aʿshā was recited:
4657 - بأَجْوَدَ مِنْه بماعُوْنِه ... إذا ما سماؤُهمُ لم تَغِمّْ
(. . . more generous than he with his utensils, when their sky does not become overcast.)
He did not mention the first object of "withholding", either because it is known, that is, "they withhold from people or from those who ask", or because the aim is to mention what they withhold and not those from whom they withhold, as a reminder of their meanness and their stinginess with trivial things, the withholding of which is held ugly by everyone.
